recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future RequestOrchestration behavior, naming, or pattern-exception changes should be handled under their own Jira keys; FHIR-13071 itself is fully represented in current build-scope source.
issue_request: FHIR-13071 was Published/Persuasive for CDS and asked that RequestGroup be aligned with the Request pattern by adding definition, basedOn, replaces, groupIdentifier, intent, and priority, and by mapping occurrence, code, supportingInfo, and performer to RequestGroup.action.timing, action.code, action.documentation, and action.participant.
initial_application: SVN r11658, preserved as git commit 416f8ff7b2637545c11170804aaffff4e866e234, explicitly applied #13071 by adding the requested RequestGroup fields, workflow mappings, bindings, and example updates. No prior AutoFHIR commit for FHIR-13071 was present on the combined branch before this reconciliation.
additional_context: FHIR-24619 later renamed RequestGroup to RequestOrchestration, and source/fhir.ini actively builds requestorchestration while mapping legacy RequestGroup references to RequestOrchestration. A 2018 canonical/uri/reference change split the original definition element into instantiatesCanonical and instantiatesUri, supported by the Zulip Request.instantiates discussion. FHIR-24619 is already represented on the combined branch and was treated as context only.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. The active RequestOrchestration StructureDefinition contains identifier, instantiatesCanonical, instantiatesUri, basedOn, replaces, groupIdentifier, status, intent, and priority with workflow mappings to the Request pattern, and maps action.code, action.documentation, action.timing[x], and action.participant to Request.code, Request.supportingInfo, Request.occurrence[x], and Request.performer. The mapping exceptions file records remaining known differences rather than indicating missing FHIR-13071 application.
